change.summary: Propagate the existing bounded failover selection signal into authentication-failure circuit and route persistence so a stalled private save cannot retain the serialized selector after the request deadline; preserve fail-closed behavior if that abandoned save later truly fails.

discarded_hypothesis.conclusion: R36's post-wait abort check already prevented a late credential acquisition after queued routing persistence; the redundant fixture was removed without changing production code.

before_implementation.observed_failure: The first request received its bounded total-deadline response, but the stalled auth-failure state save retained the routing lock so a second new request returned HTTP 503 instead of the expected HTTP 200 through the other eligible fixture account.
before_implementation.bounded_cleanup: The synthetic state-store gate was settled during fixture cleanup and the command exited normally.

late_failure_extension.observed_failure: After the partial implementation released the routing lock, a genuinely rejected late save changed readiness to 503 but the model selector still returned HTTP 200 instead of failing closed with HTTP 502.

failure_injections: an invalid synthetic credential records auth_expired and stalls its first circuit-state save beyond the 100 millisecond total deadline
the invalid SecretLease is disposed and the old selection releases the serialized routing lock
a later new request uses a different eligible fixture account while the old save remains pending
a genuine late save rejection makes both readiness and later selection fail closed without another lease or upstream contact

covers: HTTP/SSE bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
WebSocket bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
durable and abortable automatic routing plus durable manual routing
abortable credential acquisition and auth-failure persistence

qualification_invocation_notes: The first five-file focused invocation omitted the required umask 0022 and produced one state-store permission-fixture mismatch; the corrected bounded invocation passed 35/35 and is the qualifying result.

deployment.reason: The previously proven sudo root-GID transition failure and non-writable /opt/codex-account-router boundary are unchanged.

remaining_limits: 0.2.16 is verified but is not active until a host-privileged operator runs the rollback-capable router-only deployment script.

AbortSignal abandonment does not cancel an already-issued atomic state save. A different eligible account may serve a later new request while that save is pending; a genuine late rejection then makes readiness and future selection fail closed.
A process crash before the abandoned auth-failure save completes may lose that classification, so the invalid credential may be rediscovered after restart.
The timed-out request is not replayed or resumed. Only a later new request can use another eligible account.
The tests use synthetic accounts only and do not qualify a real A-to-B switch.
Real two-account verification remains blocked until explicit enrollment authorization.
